name: EBS All Expert
source_name: ICAR - National Bureau of Agricultural Insect Resources (NBAIR) / CIBRC Biocontrol Registry
evidence: Entomopathogenic fungi consortium provides biological management of sucking pests and foliar lepidopteran larvae through fungal cuticle penetration without toxic chemical residues.
safety_guidelines: Safe for pollinators when applied during early morning or late evening. Do not mix with chemical fungicides. Store below 30°C away from direct sunlight.

alternatives.name: Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) / Neem Oil 10,000 PPM
alternatives.explanation: Botanical antifeedant, repellent, and insect growth regulator (IGR). It disrupts hormonal cycles of sucking pests without killing beneficial honeybees, spiders, or ladybird beetles.
alternatives.how_to_use: Mix 50 ml of Neem Oil (or 50g NSKE) + 1 ml natural liquid soap per 10 liters of water. Spray thoroughly on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.

alternatives.name: Yellow and Blue Sticky Traps (IPM Mechanical Control)
alternatives.explanation: Chemical-free monitoring and mass trapping tool. Yellow attracts whiteflies, aphids, and leafminers; blue attracts thrips.
alternatives.how_to_use: Install 15-20 traps per acre slightly above the plant canopy level.

name: All Expert
source_name: ICAR - National Bureau of Agricultural Insect Resources (NBAIR) / CIBRC Biocontrol Registry
evidence: Triple-action bio-insecticide containing entomopathogenic fungal spores that effectively parasitize multiple insect orders with zero residue.
safety_guidelines: Store in a cool dry place away from direct sunlight. Do not mix with chemical fungicides.

alternatives.name: Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%)
alternatives.explanation: Traditional proven botanical preparation that acts as a strong feeding deterrent and inhibits egg laying of sucking insects and caterpillars.
alternatives.how_to_use: Pound 500g neem seeds, soak overnight in 10L water, filter through muslin cloth, and spray during evening hours.

alternatives.name: Dashaparni Kashayam (Fermented 10-Leaf Botanical Spray)
alternatives.explanation: Indigenous natural farming preparation made from neem, custard apple, papaya, and karanj leaves with pungent insecticidal and repellent action.
alternatives.how_to_use: Dilute 200 ml of fermented extract in 10 liters of water and spray at 10-day intervals.

name: Neem Oil / Azadirachtin
evidence: Standard botanical insecticide widely certified for organic farming. Acts as an oviposition deterrent, antifeedant, and growth disruptor.
safety_guidelines: Low toxicity to mammals and honeybees when dry; avoid spraying directly over open water bodies.

alternatives.name: Garlic-Chilli-Ginger Extract (Agniastra)
alternatives.explanation: Traditional fermented botanical extract that creates an intense pungent deterrent for hard-to-kill chewing caterpillars.
alternatives.how_to_use: Boil 500g crushed garlic, 500g green chillies, and 250g ginger in 10L cow urine. Dilute 250ml per 10L water for spraying.

name: Chlorpyrifos 20% EC
evidence: Broad-spectrum contact, stomach, and respiratory insecticide used under restricted approved label guidelines.
safety_guidelines: HIGH TOXICITY. Dangerous to aquatic life and honeybees. Restricted in many countries. Full personal protective equipment (PPE) mandatory.

alternatives.name: Metarhizium anisopliae 1% WP (Green Muscardine Fungus)
alternatives.explanation: Natural microbial bio-agent that specifically infects subterranean root grubs, termites, and cutworms. Zero toxic residue in soil and groundwater.
alternatives.how_to_use: Mix 2 kg of Metarhizium powder with 100 kg of moist farmyard manure (FYM), incubate for 7 days in shade, and incorporate into soil at sowing or earthing up.

alternatives.name: Castor Cake / Neem Cake Soil Treatment
alternatives.explanation: Natural organic oil cakes contain ricin and nimbin which repel subterranean termites and nematodes while enriching soil nitrogen.
alternatives.how_to_use: Broadcast 150-200 kg per acre into soil during land preparation.

name: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL
evidence: Systemic insecticide acting as an agonist on nicotinic acetylcholine receptors of insect nervous system.
safety_guidelines: EXTREMELY TOXIC TO HONEYBEES AND POLLINATORS. Never spray during crop flowering period. Can cause pest resurgence if overused.

alternatives.name: Verticillium lecanii 1.15% WP (Bio-Insecticide)
alternatives.explanation: Specialized bio-fungus that produces toxins which paralyze aphids, whiteflies, and mealybugs from inside. 100% safe for pollinators and honeybees.
alternatives.how_to_use: Mix 50g per 10 liters of water during high-humidity periods (above 70% RH), preferably in the late afternoon.

alternatives.name: Yellow Sticky Traps + 10,000 PPM Neem Oil Spray
alternatives.explanation: Double-action IPM: traps physically catch adult flying whiteflies, while neem prevents nymphs from molting into adults.
alternatives.how_to_use: Place 15 yellow traps per acre; spray neem oil at 3-5 ml/L every 7-10 days.

name: Mancozeb 75% WP
evidence: Multi-site contact dithiocarbamate fungicide widely registered for control of foliar fungal pathogens across agricultural crops.
safety_guidelines: Wear protective mask, gloves, and protective clothing. Observe the recommended pre-harvest interval (PHI) of 7-14 days.

alternatives.name: Trichoderma harzianum + Pseudomonas fluorescens (Bio-Shield)
alternatives.explanation: Twin bio-control agents that colonize plant leaf and stem surfaces, competing for space and nutrients to block pathogenic fungal spores.
alternatives.how_to_use: Mix 50g of each bio-agent in 10L water with 10g jaggery. Spray preventatively before disease onset.

alternatives.name: Bordeaux Mixture 1% (Copper Sulfate + Quicklime)
alternatives.explanation: Time-tested mineral preventative fungicide permitted in organic cultivation that prevents blight and mildew spore germination.
alternatives.how_to_use: Dissolve 100g Copper Sulfate and 100g Quicklime separately in water, mix to 10L, and spray immediately.

name: Trichoderma viride
source_name: Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage (PPQS)
evidence: Antagonistic beneficial fungus for seed and soil treatment that outcompetes pathogenic soil fungi and induces systemic resistance in crops.
safety_guidelines: Apply with well-decomposed organic manure; avoid concurrent use of systemic chemical fungicides.

alternatives.name: Pseudomonas fluorescens 1% WP (PGPR)
alternatives.explanation: Plant-growth-promoting rhizobacteria providing dual benefits of root disease suppression (antibiosis) and enhanced nutrient solubilization.
alternatives.how_to_use: Use 10g per kg of seeds for seed dressing, or 2.5 kg/ha mixed in compost for soil enrichment.

name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP
evidence: Broad-spectrum inorganic protectant fungicide and bactericide preventing germination of fungal and bacterial spores.
safety_guidelines: Prevent excessive application on young foliage to avoid copper phytotoxicity; do not mix with acidic compounds.

alternatives.name: Fermented Sour Buttermilk Spray (Khatti Lassi)
alternatives.explanation: Indigenous lactic acid bacteria and natural organic acids inhibit bacterial canker and mildew pathogens cleanly and at zero cost.
alternatives.how_to_use: Ferment 1 liter of fresh buttermilk with a small copper wire for 5-7 days until sour. Dilute with 10 liters of water and spray.

name: Carbendazim 50% WP
evidence: Systemic fungicide interfering with fungal spindle formation during cell division. Known for high chemical persistence.
safety_guidelines: Classified as toxic to endocrine and reproductive systems. Avoid water runoff into fish ponds.

alternatives.name: Trichoderma viride + Seed Soaking in Beejamrutha
alternatives.explanation: Natural cow-urine and lime concoction with antagonistic bio-fungus for seed coating; prevents blast and smut without toxic fungicides.
alternatives.how_to_use: Treat 1 kg of seed with 10g Trichoderma powder before sowing.

name: Glyphosate 41% SL
evidence: Inhibits EPSP synthase in plants, preventing amino acid synthesis. Restricted to designated non-crop areas in India.
safety_guidelines: RESTRICTED HERBICIDE. Do not spray over standing food crops. Wear protective respirator and rubber boots.

alternatives.name: Live Legume Cover Cropping (Cowpea / Sunnhemp)
alternatives.explanation: Dense cover crops smother weeds, prevent weed seed germination by blocking sunlight, and fix 40-60 kg of atmospheric nitrogen per acre.
alternatives.how_to_use: Broadcast 15-20 kg/acre between crop rows or during fallow periods.

alternatives.name: Straw Mulching / Plastic Mulch Film
alternatives.explanation: Physical weed barrier that blocks weed emergence while conserving 30-40% soil moisture.
alternatives.how_to_use: Apply a 4-inch layer of dry paddy straw between crop rows.

name: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)
evidence: Microbial crystal proteins (Cry toxins) dissolve in insect alkaline gut, selectively killing caterpillar larvae while being harmless to humans, birds, and honeybees.
safety_guidelines: Apply during evening hours because UV sunlight degrades Bt crystals rapidly.

alternatives.name: Helicoverpa NPV (Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus) + Pheromone Traps
alternatives.explanation: Highly targeted viral biological control for caterpillar pests with zero chemical footprint.
alternatives.how_to_use: Spray 250 LE (Larval Equivalents)/ha mixed with 0.1% jaggery during evening hours.

name: Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG
evidence: Semi-synthetic avermectin derived from fermentation of Streptomyces avermitilis. Interacts with GABA receptors causing caterpillar paralysis.
safety_guidelines: Wait 3-5 days after spraying before harvesting edible fruits. Keep away from water bodies.

alternatives.name: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) + Neem Oil 10,000 PPM
alternatives.explanation: Combined biological treatment: Neem deters feeding and egg laying, while Bt eliminates existing larvae without chemical resistance.
alternatives.how_to_use: Mix 2g Bt + 3 ml Neem Oil per liter of water. Spray directly into plant whorls.
